newsitem.title: FRANCE: France expels three Malian former hunger strikers.
newsitem.headline: France expels three Malian former hunger strikers.

text.p: France has expelled three Malian immigrants who took part in a seven-week hunger strike in a Paris church last summer to demand the right to stay, a group which monitors expulsions said on Friday.
The Cimade group named the three, whom it said were expelled on an Air France plane to Bamako on Thursday, as Sidy Diarra, Karounga Diagouraga and Moussa Sissoko.
The Interior Ministry had no comment on the report.
A total of 10 hunger strikers were among some 220 people ejected from the Saint Bernard Church in central Paris in August where they were staging a sit-in.
Many immigrants say they once enjoyed residence rights but were pushed into illegality when laws were stiffened in 1993 to curb immigration.

A Cimade spokesman said two other former hunger strikers, Lamin Dembele and Sema Camara, who had also been taken to Roissy-Charles de Gaulle airport north of Paris, had been brought back to the capital but were likely to be expelled soon.
The five Malians were detained by police when they called at police headquarters in Paris on Thursday.
Roissy airport officials said the Bamako plane took off more than two hours late because of delays due to a demonstration by a dozen supporters and to a false bomb alert.
The government has said the protesters have no legal right to stay in France but their cases would be reviewed individually on humanitarian grounds.
